clue.text: Does it only illuminate the port side?

definitions.text: Does it only illuminate the port side?

parts.words: Does it only illuminate the port side?
parts.note: the question plays on 'port side', the left of a ship, while meaning a lamp that guides vessels into a harbour

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a lamp that lights only the left-hand side of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port side' suggests the nautical left; the beacon in question shines at the port itself, marking the harbour entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A beacon set at a harbour entrance guides ships safely into port.

clue.text: Affirms horse on the outside had the bag

indicators.note: the horse word sits on the outside, wrapped round the word for affirms

parts.note: a hack is a horse for ordinary riding
avers means affirms or declares

explanation.surface: Someone vouches that the horse outside was carrying the bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' tempts as the definition's subject; it is the outside piece, split in two around the word for affirms.
explanation.definitionFit: A knapsack slung over the shoulder is a bag used by walkers and soldiers.

clue.text: Arcadian suggesting the countryside

explanation.surface: An idyllic place that brings fields and farms to mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Arcadia, a region of ancient Greece, became the poets' byword for simple country life.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia is the classical pastoral idyll, so Arcadian means pastoral, and anything evoking farmland and villages is likewise of the country.

clue.text: Old side yet to be paid

parts.note: a wing is a side, as of a building or a team

explanation.surface: An old team whose wages are still outstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt still outstanding is due, not yet settled.

clue.text: Got on well with maitre d'hotel, not him strangely enough

indicators.note: not says some letters, those of the word him, are left out of the pool
strangely says the remaining letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written
the letters removed from the fodder

explanation.surface: A diner found the head waiter congenial, oddly enough not the waiter himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove H, I and M from MAITRE D'HOTEL and rearrange the remaining nine letters ('strangely enough').
explanation.definitionFit: To have an affinity or rapport with someone is to get on well with them.

clue.text: Lack of proportion I am to compare

parts.note: contracted to I'm
to balance two things is to weigh or compare them

explanation.surface: Someone admits to a lopsided habit of comparing.
explanation.definitionFit: Disproportion is an unequal state where things are out of balance.

clue.text: Some sharp young eagle

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A keen-eyed juvenile bird of prey.
explanation.definitionFit: The harpy is a large South American eagle, one of the most powerful raptors.

clue.text: Late although there's time for one more round

definitions.text: there's time for one more round

explanation.surface: A drinker reasons it is late, yet there is still time for one more round.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading recalls old British pub closing time at eleven, the last moment for another round of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: The last possible moment is late, and it is also, literally, the hour before old pub closing when one last round is possible.

clue.text: Suitor's first lady had too much

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word lady

parts.note: to have had too much is to go over the limit

explanation.surface: A suitor's first lady drank to excess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first lady' tempts with EVE; here first just picks L from lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooer courting someone is an admirer or sweetheart.

clue.text: Stingy liar be ill, suffering

indicators.note: suffering suggests the letters are in a bad way, knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A mean liar falls sick and suffers.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow-minded meanness, ungenerous in spirit or with money, is the sense of stingy here.

clue.text: Big in the middle? That's generous

parts.note: large means big
having a heart, the centre or middle of something, playfully read as hearted

explanation.surface: A remark about someone with a big middle being called generous.
explanation.walkthrough: A large heart is a big middle, and big-hearted people are kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindly and magnanimous people are open-handed with others.

clue.text: Pretty unimportant flare

explanation.surface: A flare that matters little.
explanation.definitionFit: Something only slight is of little weight, while a Very light is a coloured signal flare fired from a pistol, named after its inventor Edward Very.

clue.text: Flat covering for hen

explanation.surface: A flat sheet put down for a chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: A coating spread flat over a surface is one sense, and a hen kept for eggs is the other.

clue.text: Sandy travelling took another man into the old country

indicators.note: into puts the second man's name inside the scrambled letters
travelling suggests the letters of Sandy move about

parts.note: Alan is a man's name, another besides Sandy

explanation.surface: Sandy, on his travels, takes a second man with him to the old homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: Nyasaland was the British colonial name, before 1964, of what is now Malawi.
explanation.definitionFit: Nyasaland was the colonial-era name of the African state now called Malawi, a former country.

clue.text: Plant from Andorra's round in the middle

indicators.note: in the middle places the round letter within the rearranged letters
from says the plant is made out of these letters, reworked

parts.note: the letters of Andorra's, possessive s included as a letter
a round shape looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A plant that grows in a round patch in the middle of Andorra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' signals rearranging the eight letters of Andorra's, the possessive s counting as a letter, and 'in the middle' sets the round letter inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Aaron's rod is a name for the great mullein, a tall yellow-flowered plant.

clue.text: Pledge of security

explanation.surface: A promise that brings safety.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm promise is one sense, and freedom from doubt or a sense of safety and confidence is the other.

clue.text: Fertiliser can upside down and touching

indicators.note: in a down light upside down would flip; across, it reads the can word backwards

parts.note: a tin is a can
re means about or concerning, touching on

explanation.surface: A can of fertiliser turned upside down and touching the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is used as a plant food and in gunpowder.

clue.text: Attempted to include faction that had split up

indicators.note: to include says the faction word goes inside the attempted word

parts.note: tried means attempted
a sect is a faction or breakaway group

explanation.surface: An effort to bring in a faction that had broken away.
explanation.definitionFit: Divided into three parts is a precise form of being divided.

clue.text: Walker be president in a short time

indicators.note: in puts the president inside the short time

parts.note: hr is the short form of hour, a time
Ike was the nickname of US President Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A rambler hopes to become president before long.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rambles on foot through the countryside is a walker.

clue.text: Chimney hat

explanation.surface: A chimney that doubles as a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal pipe carrying smoke from a stove is one sense, and a tall cylindrical silk hat is the other.

clue.text: Ancient penny once held by lone ranger

indicators.note: held by puts the penny inside the rearranged letters
ranger, one who roams, suggests the letters of lone wander

parts.note: d was the abbreviation for a penny in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: An old coin kept by a cowboy hero riding alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lone ranger' evokes the masked cowboy; 'ranger' scrambles LONE to OLEN, holding D.
explanation.definitionFit: Of bygone days, as in olden times, means very old.

clue.text: Motorists do go round lizard

indicators.note: go round says the word do encircles the motorists

parts.note: taken as written
the RAC, Royal Automobile Club, is a British motorists' organisation

explanation.surface: Drivers swerve around a lizard on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Draco is the genus of gliding flying lizards of Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Storyteller or artist against true version

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, stands for an artist
con means against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: a version is a rendering, so the letters of true are rendered anew

explanation.surface: A storyteller or a painter offers a version contrary to the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a skilled teller of anecdotes, a narrator.

clue.text: This side of the city for bargains?

definitions.text: This side of the city for bargains?

parts.words: This side of the city for bargains?
parts.note: the clue points at a famous old market street in the City of London whose name is a word for low-priced plus side

explanation.surface: Asking which part of town has the best deals.
explanation.walkthrough: The street in the City of London that was its medieval market splits as a word for bargain-priced followed by 'side'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bargains are low-priced, inexpensive goods.

clue.text: Ulster certainly third more attractive

parts.note: NI, Northern Ireland, is often called Ulster

indicators.note: third takes the first third of the nine-letter word certainly, its opening three letters

explanation.surface: Ulster is certainly a third more appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasanter or more pleasing is a comparative of agreeable.

clue.text: Back-boiler put back in order

parts.note: rear means back
a range is a cooking stove that may heat water, a kind of boiler

explanation.surface: A back-boiler is reinstalled in its proper place.
explanation.walkthrough: A back-boiler is a water heater behind a fireplace; split it into its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To reorder or sort differently is to put things in a new arrangement.

clue.text: Share that is due to a smart girl

parts.note: a cut is a share of proceeds
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A share of the money is owed to a clever girl.
explanation.definitionFit: An attractive, pretty young woman is a cute one, informally.

clue.text: Having sound adjusted is not easily annoyed

parts.note: sound means good, in good condition
tempered means moderated or adjusted, as a tuned instrument is

explanation.surface: Having one's hearing aid adjusted makes a person calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Equable people with a calm disposition rarely lose their cool.
